tool.name: Hydrostatic balance
tool.measures: the weight of the stone in water, and its density
tool.where: Gemmology House and Office, top row, near the loupe
tips: Weigh the stone in air first

steps.title: Archimedes' principle
steps.text: Dipped in water, a stone seems lighter: the water pushes it upwards. This push is equal to the weight of the water displaced. The denser the stone, the less the push relieves it compared with its weight.

steps.title: Two weighings
steps.text: 1. Weigh the stone in air (carat balance): P air. 2. Put it in the basket dipped in water: the balance gives P water. The stone must be quite dry at the start, with no air bubble stuck to it.

steps.title: The density
steps.text: Density is worked out from the two weights: d = P air ÷ (P air − P water) For example, 2.00 ct in air and 1.45 ct in water give 2.00 ÷ 0.55 ≈ 3.64. Since you have already weighed the stone, the balance does the calculation on its own.

steps.title: Reading the density
steps.text:
Each species has its own density: quartz around 2.65, beryl 2.7, corundum 4.0, diamond 3.52, garnet 3.6 to 4.3.

Density alone is not enough: several species look alike. It is by crossing measurements that you get the answer.
